_doc: Per-subcategory scope-selection + read-across config for the Cat-1 compiler. Every number the compiler emits traces to a register row selected by these rules. scope_include/exclude are case-insensitive regex fragments tested against product_scope. read_across names the register row for the nearest analogous government value where no government regulates the exact product. Audited configs for rows 2-9 are filled by the build workflow; formula-powder (row 1) is the regression anchor, calibrated to reproduce the deployed, audited standard.

_read_across_canon.tHg: cn_thg_canned-complementary-foods-for-infants-a_20 — China GB 2762 total-Hg 20 for canned complementary infant foods; no government sets a mercury ML for these product forms anywhere.
_read_across_canon.Cr: china_gb2762_cr_milk_powder_2000 — China GB 2762 total-Cr 2000 for milk powder; dairy read-across. For non-dairy subcategories the nearest analogous Cr source may differ; the workflow adjudicates per subcategory.
_read_across_canon.Cr-VI: not-material: reflex speciation under total-Cr; any quantifiable Cr-VI fails.

MeHg.control: Methylmercury is not a distinct accumulation pathway in non-marine infant foods. Total mercury is measured on every lot and bounds the methylmercury fraction; reflex MeHg speciation is required when source materials include fish or another credible methylation pathway.
MeHg.reference_method: Total Hg by EPA 7473 or ICP-MS; MeHg by species-specific GC-ICP-MS / HPLC-ICP-MS when the matrix contains fish or total Hg approaches the category ceiling.

Cr-VI.control: Total chromium is measured on every lot. Any total-Cr result at or above 100 ug/kg triggers Cr(VI) speciation, and any quantifiable Cr(VI) fails certification.
Cr-VI.reference_method: Total Cr by ICP-MS; Cr(VI) by EPA 3060A alkaline extraction with IC-ICP-MS (EPA 6800 / EN 15192 or equivalent).

baby-cereals-dry-rice-based.name: Baby cereals / grain products, dry (rice-based)
scope_include: infant milk substitute and infant foods

tHg.label: government read-across — Israel FCS-2016 porridges & other foods for infants and toddlers, total-Hg 8 (the strictest applicable baby-food mercury ML; supersedes the looser China canned-complementary 20).

Cr.control: No government sets a total-chromium ML for any non-dairy infant food; the dairy milk-powder read-across (China 2000) is a weak analogy for a grain cereal. Cr(III) is nutritionally essential and Cr(VI) reduces to Cr(III) in-matrix, so total-Cr is not a material toxic in this matrix. Firm control: reflex speciation — any total-Cr result >= 100 ug/kg triggers Cr(VI) speciation, and any quantifiable Cr(VI) fails.
Cr.reference_method: Total-Cr screen by ICP-MS; on any result >= 100 ug/kg, Cr(VI) speciation by EPA 3060A alkaline digestion + IC-ICP-MS (or equivalent); LOQ-level quantifiable Cr(VI) = fail.

Al.label: government read-across (AU-NZ Schedule 19 infant-formula Al 500, the only government aluminium ML in any jurisdiction) applied at face value; the 8:1 reconstitution factor is formula-specific and is not applied to a non-formula product.

non-root-vegetable-purees.name: Non-root vegetable purees
non-root-vegetable-purees._basis_note: Product is a wet, ready-to-eat non-root vegetable puree (jar/pouch/tub); its physical native basis is as_consumed. native_basis is deliberately set to as_sold because every applicable government limit (EU/UK/IN baby-food MLs, China canned-complementary tHg read-across) is set on this same wet product but tagged basis_class=as_sold in the register, and the compiler's 8:1 powder-reconstitution factor must NOT be applied to any of them. Setting native_basis=as_consumed makes the compiler wrongly divide those wet MLs by 8, inventing six sub-legal numbers (Pb 2.5, iAs 2.5, Cd 5, Ni 63, Sn 630, tHg 2.5) that no government sets. Trade-off: the as_sold setting instead ×8-inflates the one read-across source tagged as_consumed (AU-NZ Al) -> see Al flag.

tHg.label: government read-across — Israel FCS-2016 porridges & other foods for infants and toddlers, total-Hg 8 (the strictest applicable baby-food mercury ML; supersedes the looser China canned-complementary 20).

Cr.reference_method: EPA 3060A alkaline digestion + IC-ICP-MS for Cr-VI; ICP-MS for total Cr

meat-and-poultry-purees.name: Meat and poultry purées for infants and young children

tAs.label: Sovereign ingredient-matrix read-across from the MERCOSUR 500 ug/kg total-arsenic maximum for raw bovine, ovine, porcine, caprine and poultry meats. No government total-arsenic maximum for finished meat baby food is loaded.

tHg.label: Sovereign infant-food read-across from Israel's 8 ug/kg total-mercury maximum for porridges and other foods for infants and toddlers.

Sn.label: India FSSAI non-canned infant-food total-tin maximum (5000 ug/kg), applied at face value.

Al.label: Conservative sovereign infant-food read-across from the AU-NZ non-soy infant-formula aluminium maximum (500 ug/kg).

Cr.control: Total Cr remains mandatory. Any result at or above 100 ug/kg triggers Cr(VI) speciation, and any quantifiable Cr(VI) fails; no sovereign meat-purée total-Cr maximum is loaded.
Cr.reference_method: Total Cr by ICP-MS; Cr(VI) by validated alkaline extraction and IC-ICP-MS.

Pb.label: Direct EU maximum for baby food for infants and young children (20 ug/kg). The explicit lookup avoids treating the regulation's 'except ... formula' wording as a product-scope exclusion.

tAs.label: Sovereign ingredient-matrix read-across from Singapore's 1000 ug/kg total-arsenic maximum for fish, crustaceans and molluscs. No government total-arsenic maximum for finished fish-containing baby food is loaded.

tHg.label: Sovereign infant-food read-across from Israel's 8 ug/kg total-mercury maximum. This is stricter than the seafood mercury tier and therefore governs the finished baby food.

MeHg.label: Seafood-component methylmercury comparator from Mexico NOM-242 (500 ug/kg for other fishery products). The compiler reconciles it against the much stricter finished-product total-Hg ceiling, so MeHg is explicitly bounded by tHg rather than omitted.

Sn.label: India FSSAI non-canned infant-food total-tin maximum (5000 ug/kg), applied at face value.

Al.label: Conservative sovereign infant-food read-across from the AU-NZ non-soy infant-formula aluminium maximum (500 ug/kg).

Cr.label: India FSSAI total-chromium maximum for all fishery products (12000 ug/kg), read across to the fish component of the finished baby food.

_method_note: 8:1 reconstitution applies ONLY to formula subcategories (reconstitution_8to1:true). All other subcategories take government MLs and read-across values at face value. Read-across is always face value (nearest basis-appropriate government row).
